35-046.r: NHRC purview (Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993) → rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity, guaranteed by Constitution or international covenants and enforceable by Indian courts.
35-046.c: No answer printed and MPPSC deleted it; the explanation lists equality, then says 'education' instead, so it is garbled.

35-047.r: 'Public Servant' in Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 → defined in Section 2(M); same meaning as Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.

35-048.r: 'Armed forces' under Protection of Human Rights Act → naval, military and air forces and other armed forces of the Union; armed forces of the State not included.

35-049.r: NHRC selection committee (Section 4, Act 1993) → PM, Lok Sabha Speaker, Union Home Minister, LoPs of both Houses, Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha; Chairman of Rajya Sabha not included.
35-049.t: Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha is a member; the Chairman of Rajya Sabha is not.
hi: National Human Rights Commission (राष्ट्रीय मानवाधिकार आयोग)

35-051.r: NHRC → statutory body (1993); chairman (retired CJI or SC judge) + four members; 6 ex-officio members; Law Commission Chairperson is not an ex-officio member.

35-052.r: NHRC Chairperson and members (2019 amendment) → term three years or until age 70, whichever earlier; not eligible for further government employment.
35-052.c: No answer printed; after the 2019 amendment options (a), (b) and (c) are all incorrect, so no single answer.

35-053.r: NHRC Chairperson → term of 3 years or until age seventy, whichever is earlier.

35-054.r: NHRC Chairman and members → 3 years or until age 70, whichever earlier; afterwards not eligible for Central or State government employment.
35-054.c: Book gives no single answer (*): the term is now three years; when this was asked (2018) it was five years or age 70, i.e. option (b).

35-055.r: NHRC → powers only recommendatory; at least one woman member (civil-society members raised from two to three); Chairman: former CJI or SC judge (2019); SHRCs separate.
35-055.c: No answer printed; now only statements 3 and 4 are true, and no option gives that pair.

35-056.r: NHRC Chairman → former CJI or a Supreme Court Judge (2019 Amendment); term 3 years or age 70 → A ('only former CJI') and R ('5 years') both false.

35-058.r: First NHRC Chairman → Justice Ranganath Misra (12 October 1993 to 24 November 1996); NHRC set up 12 October 1993.

35-059.r: Justice H.L. Dattu → NHRC Chairman from 29.02.2016 to 02.12.2020; Justice V. Ramasubramanian chairman since 30/12/2024.

35-060.r: State Human Rights Commission Chairperson → Chief Justice or a Judge of the High Court (Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019).

35-061.r: SHRC Chairperson and members → appointed by Governor on recommendation of CM (chair), Assembly Speaker, State Home Minister, LoP in Assembly (+ Council Chairman and LoP if Council exists).
hi: State Human Rights Commission (राज्य मानवाधिकार आयोग)

35-063.r: SHRC selection committee (Section 22, Act 1993) → chaired by Chief Minister; Governor is not on it, he only appoints.

35-065.r: SHRC selection committee includes → Speaker of Legislative Assembly and Leader of Opposition; not the Governor or High Court Chief Justice.
35-065.c: Explanation reads '& (c)': Leader of Opposition (c) is also a member, but the book prints only (a).

35-066.r: Sitting High Court Judge or sitting District Judge → made SHRC member only after consulting the Chief Justice of that State's High Court.

35-067.r: Vacancy or absence of SHRC Chairperson → Governor authorises one member to act as Chairperson.

35-068.r: NHRC functions (Section 12, Act 1993) → promote research in human rights and encourage NGOs working in the field; both statements true.

35-069.r: State Human Rights Commission → can inquire suo motu, visit jails, review human-rights protection; cannot punish violators.
35-069.t: Human Rights Commissions only recommend; they have no power to punish.

35-070.r: SHRC annual report → to the State Government; laid before State Legislature with action-taken memorandum and reasons for non-acceptance.
35-070.t: Not the Governor: SHRC reports go to the State Government.

35-071.r: Members and officers of NHRC/SHRC acting under Protection of Human Rights Act → deemed Public Servants (Section 21 IPC).

35-072.r: Special Public Prosecutor for a Human Rights Court → advocate with at least 7 years' practice, specified by State Government (Section 31, Act 1993).

35-073.r: For offences under IPC Sections 175, 178, 179, 180 and 228 → Human Rights Commission deemed a Civil Court; it has all powers of a civil court.

35-074.r: Human rights complaints against armed forces → Commission only seeks a report from the Central Government and makes recommendations (limited role).

35-075.r: Human Rights Commission → non-constitutional (Act of 1993). Constitutional: State Finance Commission (Art 243-I), Lok Sabha Secretariat (Art 98), Finance Commission (Art 280).

35-076.r: NHRC → non-constitutional (statutory); Backward Class Commission (Art 340, NCBC Art 338B), Finance Commission (Art 280), Election Commission (Art 324) → constitutional.

35-077.r: Wrong pair: National Development Council → 1952, not 1954. Correct: Inter-State Council 1990, Central Vigilance Commission 1964, NHRC 1993.

35-078.r: First Law Commission of independent India (1955) → Chairman M.C. Setalvad, then Attorney General.

35-079.r: National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution → 22 February 2000, Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah; recommendatory; not approved by Parliament; last report 31 March 2002.

35-081.r: Central Pollution Control Board Chairman → nominated by Central Government: an expert in environmental protection; not President, PM, Vice-President or Environment Minister.
35-081.c: No answer printed: none of the options is correct, so MPPSC dropped the question.

35-082.r: Swarn Singh Committee (1976) → priority of Directive Principles over Fundamental Rights; led to 42nd Amendment; found Presidential system unsuitable for India.

35-083.r: Central Vigilance Commission → recommended by Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962-64); first neither constitutional nor statutory; later made statutory by Parliament.

35-084.r: CVC → based on K. Santhanam Committee (appointed 1962); CVC set up 1964; statutory status by Parliament's law in 2003.

35-085.r: Central Vigilance Commission (1964) → Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption. Kelkar Committee → review of PPP model.

35-086.r: CVC → in no Article of the Constitution; set up February 1964 (K. Santhanam); statutory since September 2003. Art 280 → Finance Commission; Art 276 → profession tax.

35-087.r: Wrong pairs: Prevention of Corruption Act → 1988 (not 1985); Enforcement Directorate → 1956 (not 2000). Correct: CBI 1963, CVC 1964.
35-087.c: Book prints two answers, (c) and (d), since both pairs are wrong.

35-088.r: Mandal Commission (1979) → set up by Janata Party Government of PM Morarji Desai; headed by Bindheshwari Prasad Mandal; to identify socially and educationally backward persons.

35-089.r: Mandal Commission → constituted 1979 by Janata Party Government, chaired by B.P. Mandal; report submitted in 1980.

35-090.r: Causes of atrocities on SCs and STs (National Commission report, 1990) → land disputes, alienation of tribal land, bonded labour, indebtedness, non-payment of minimum wages; not religious causes.

35-091.r: Public Service Commissions for Union and States → Article 315; Articles 315 to 323 in Part XIV cover UPSC and State PSCs.

35-092.r: UPSC has nothing to do with State Public Service Commissions: it does not supervise them or send them guidelines.

35-093.r: Union Public Service Commission → a constitutional body, formed under Article 315.

35-094.r: UPSC functions come from → the Constitution (Art 320), Parliamentary laws (Art 321), executive rules and orders, and conventions → all four.

35-095.r: UPSC annual report → to the President (Art 323); laid before each House with a memorandum on cases where its advice was not accepted.

35-096.r: Joint State PSC [Art 315(2)] → when two or more States agree (resolution by each House of their legislatures) and Parliament provides for it by law → both.

35-098.r: Chairman and members of a Joint PSC (or UPSC) → appointed by the President; of a State PSC → by the Governor [Art 316(1)].
35-098.t: A Joint PSC serves States, yet its Chairman is appointed by the President, not the Governors.

35-099.r: State PSC Chairman and members → appointed by the Governor (Articles 315 to 323, Part XIV).

35-100.r: State PSC members → appointed by the Governor; UPSC Chairman and members → by the President [Art 316(1)].

35-102.r: Removal of a PSC Chairman or member → Article 317: by President on ground of misbehaviour, after Supreme Court inquiry on President's reference (Art 145 procedure).
35-102.h: 315 create, 316 appoint, 317 remove: count up the life of a PSC member.

35-104.r: Rajasthan PSC → Chairman and members appointed by the Governor; removable only by the President → both statements correct.
35-104.t: Governor appoints State PSC members but cannot remove them; only the President can.

35-105.r: Mandatory PSC consultation on disciplinary matters of civil servants → Art 320(3)(c). Art 318 → service regulations; Art 322 → expenses; Art 325 → elections.

35-107.r: UPSC Chairman → removed by the President [Art 317(1)] for misbehaviour after a Supreme Court inquiry (Art 145 procedure).

35-108.r: State PSC is not consulted on individual transfers of civil servants; it is consulted on recruitment methods and principles of appointment, promotion and inter-service transfers (Art 320).
35-108.t: Principles for transfer from one service to another → consulted; actual transfers → not consulted.

35-109.r: UPSC can serve a State's needs → if the Governor requests, with approval of the President [Art 315(4)].

35-111.r: Functions of UP Public Service Commission → can be extended by Uttar Pradesh State Legislature by law (Art 321); UPSC's by Parliament.

35-112.r: Expenses of Union and State Public Service Commissions → Article 322.

35-113.r: UP PSC expenses → charged on Consolidated Fund of the State; UPSC's → Consolidated Fund of India (Art 322). State PSC annual report → Governor [Art 323(2)].

35-114.r: Rajasthan Public Service Commission → presents its annual report to the Governor of Rajasthan.

35-115.r: First Public Service Commission → under Government of India Act, 1919; set up 1 October 1926 (Chairman + four members); became Federal PSC under 1935 Act.

35-116.r: Madhya Pradesh PSC → constituted by the President under Section 118(3) of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.

35-117.r: Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission → maximum five members. Art 318 → regulations on service conditions of PSC members and staff.

35-118.r: First woman Chairman of UPSC → Roze Millian Bethew (1992 to 1996).

35-119.r: Bureaucracy in India → agency for implementing public policy; it builds the political executive's credibility with people.

35-120.r: Doctrine of Pleasure → Article 310: Union and defence services hold office at the President's pleasure; State services at the Governor's pleasure.

35-122.r: P.C. Hota Committee on Civil Services Reforms → constituted February 2004; report within six months.

35-123.r: Civil Services Day → 21 April (first held 21 April 2006, Vigyan Bhawan); on 21 April 1947 Sardar Patel addressed the first batch at Metcalf House.

36-001.r: Special provisions for different States → Articles 371 to 371-J (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, Karnataka).

36-002.r: Article 371-B → special provisions for (tribal areas of) Assam; Part XXI (temporary, transitional and special provisions).

36-003.r: Article 371 → special provisions for Maharashtra and Gujarat.

36-004.r: Article 371-J (Ninety-Eighth Amendment, 2012) → Governor of Karnataka to develop the Hyderabad-Karnataka region.

36-005.r: Only State with its own separate Constitution → Jammu and Kashmir (Art 370); Art 370 made inoperative 6 August 2019; now J&K and Ladakh are UTs.

36-006.r: Special Category Status (Gadgil Formula) → hilly terrain, low population density or large tribal population, international border, backwardness, weak finances; 'sizeable SC and ST population' is not one.
hi: Special Category Status (विशेष श्रेणी का दर्जा)

36-007.r: J&K special status (Art 370) → it had its own separate Constitution and was outside the Art 152 definition of States; became a Union Territory on 31 October 2019.

36-008.r: Article 370 (Jammu and Kashmir) → a temporary and transitional provision; abrogated 6 August 2019.

36-010.r: Articles applying on their own to J&K (then) → Art 1 (integral part of India) and Art 370 (special status). Now J&K and Ladakh are UTs.

36-011.r: J&K special status → Article 370 (now ended). Art 360 → Financial Emergency; Art 1 → Union of States; Art 270 → shared taxes.

36-012.r: Sadr-e-Riyasat renamed Governor in J&K → Sixth Amendment Act, 1965 of the J&K Constitution; Karn Singh was first Sadr-e-Riyasat (1951).
36-012.c: No answer printed: the correct year 1965 is not among the options.

36-013.r: Order → Instrument of Accession (26 October 1947) → Constitution of India enforced (1950) → J&K Assembly ratified accession (17 November 1956) → J&K Constitution in force (26 January 1957).
36-013.c: Explanation says India's Constitution was enforced on '26 November, 1950', a slip; the order I, II, III, IV still holds.

36-014.r: Never given Special Category Status → Bihar. Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir had it; 11 states in all.

37-001.r: Election Commission → Article 324: superintendence, direction and control of electoral rolls and elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President.

37-003.r: Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners → appointed by the President [Art 324(2)], subject to law made by Parliament.

37-004.r: Wrong: Law Commission settles differences among Election Commissioners → decided by majority. ECs removed only on CEC's recommendation; all have equal powers; term 6 years or age 65.

37-005.r: Election Commission → advisory role in post-election disqualification of sitting MPs (Art 103) and MLAs (Art 192). Set up 25 January 1950; two more ECs from 1 October 1993.

37-006.r: CEC and Election Commissioners → equal powers and equal salary (same as SC Judge); CEC removed like an SC Judge; term 6 years or age 65 (not five years/62).

37-007.r: CEC → salary equal to SC Judge; term 6 years or age 65, whichever first; resignation addressed to the President, not to the CEC → (i) and (ii) correct.

37-010.r: Chief Election Commissioner → ranks 9(A) in Table of Precedence, with UPSC Chairperson and CAG. CJI and Lok Sabha Speaker → 6th; Governor → 4th.
37-010.c: No answer printed: none of the options (CJI, Governor, Lok Sabha Speaker, State Speaker) matches the CEC's rank.

37-011.r: Elections entrusted to independent Election Commission (Art 324) (A true); CEC removed like SC Judge, other ECs by President with CEC's advice (R true); R doesn't explain A.

37-013.r: An Election Commissioner → removed by the President only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
37-013.t: CEC is removed like a Supreme Court Judge; other Election Commissioners only on CEC's recommendation.

37-014.r: Election Commission [Art 324(1)] → electoral rolls and elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, President, Vice-President; it does not recommend President's Rule or make election laws.

37-016.r: Local body (Panchayat, municipality) elections → State Election Commission (Arts 243K, 243ZA), not the Election Commission of India.

37-017.r: Not ECI's work: electing Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Deputy Chairman (done by House members); municipal polls (State Election Commission, Art 243ZA); election disputes (judiciary) → none.

37-019.r: ECI → three-member body (CEC + two ECs), not five; ECI (not Home Ministry) fixes election schedules; ECI resolves split/merger disputes of recognised parties → only 3 true.

37-020.r: Election notification → issued by President (Parliament) and Governor (State Legislature), not by Election Commission; EC allots symbols and conducts polls.

37-021.r: Start of election process → Election Commission recommends; President or Governor issues notification; then EC announces dates and timings.

37-022.r: Election systems in India → direct election on adult suffrage (Lok Sabha, Assemblies) and proportional representation by single transferable vote (President, VP, Rajya Sabha, Councils); no list or cumulative system.

37-023.r: Disqualification of MPs → decided by the President after obtaining the Election Commission's opinion and acting on it (Article 103).

37-025.r: Article 103 → before deciding disqualification of an MP [Art 102(1) grounds], the President must obtain the Election Commission's opinion.

37-026.r: Winner losing his deposit → a very large number of candidates contested; deposit is lost if a candidate gets no more than one-sixth of valid votes.

37-027.r: Disqualification of convicted persons → by Parliament: Section 8(3), RPA 1951: jailed 2 years or more → disqualified from conviction until 6 years after release.

37-028.r: Model Code of Conduct → applies once Election Commission announces schedule (A true); framed by Election Commission, not enacted by Parliament (R false).
hi: Model Code of Conduct (आदर्श आचार संहिता)

37-029.r: Right to vote and to be elected in India → a legal right (not fundamental, constitutional or natural).

37-030.r: Right to vote and right to be elected → legal rights under an Act (ordinary law), not Fundamental or Constitutional Rights.

37-031.r: Right to vote → merely a statutory (legal) right; Kuldip Nayar vs Union of India: neither fundamental nor constitutional right.
37-031.t: Don't pick 'Constitutional Right': the Court called voting a statutory right.

37-032.r: Voting age 21 → 18 by 61st Amendment Act, 1988 (in force 28 March 1989); first used in the November 1989 Lok Sabha general election.

37-036.r: Adult suffrage → Article 326: elections to Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage.

37-037.r: Right to vote (adult suffrage) for electing Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha → Article 326.

37-038.r: Voting age → 18 years: 61st Amendment Act, 1988 amended Art 326 (from 21); Representation of the People Act, 1951 amended too.

37-039.r: Postal ballot from home for senior citizens → age raised from 80 to 85 years (Rule 27A, Conduct of Elections Rules 1961, amended 1 March 2024); also 40% disabled.

37-040.r: State Legislature elections → adult suffrage; one electoral roll per territorial constituency; no bar of religion, race, sex on roll; parties free to have norms → all four.

37-041.r: 'One Nation One Election' → needs amendment of Articles 83, 85, 172, 174 and 356 → more than one option.

37-042.r: Simultaneous Elections committee (2 September 2023) → chair Ram Nath Kovind; members incl. Amit Shah, N.K. Singh, Subhash C. Kashyap, Harish Salve; Niten Chandra Secretary; Tushar Mehta not on it.
37-042.c: Explanation ends by naming Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury (not an option) as the non-member; Tushar Mehta is simply absent from its list.

37-043.r: Exit Poll → survey of voters after voting on whom they voted for. Opinion Poll → survey before the election.
37-043.t: Don't confuse exit poll (after voting) with opinion poll (before the election).

37-044.r: Lok Sabha elections 2009 → total electors 714 million.

37-045.r: RPA 1951 (Section 33) → max two Lok Sabha constituencies (1 false). Devi Lal contested three in 1991 (2 true). No rule makes party pay bypoll costs (3 false).

37-046.r: RPA (Amendment) Act 1996 → insulting National Flag/Constitution: six-year disqualification; higher security deposit; no countermanding on a candidate's death; max two constituencies, not one.
37-046.t: Statement 3 was wrong: the limit is two constituencies, not one.

37-047.r: Dinesh Goswami Committee (electoral reforms; Goswami was Law Minister, 1989) → recommended government funding of parliamentary elections; basis of RPA Amendment, 1996.

37-049.r: Lok Sabha → 84 SC and 47 ST seats of 543 (Delimitation 2008), not 44 ST. Delimitation Commission picks reserved seats; Central Government constitutes it, not Speaker.

37-050.r: Delimitation Commission orders → cannot be challenged in court; laid before Lok Sabha or State Assembly but cannot be modified → both true.

37-051.r: Delimitation Commissions under Delimitation Acts → four: 1952, 1963, 1973, 2002; the 2020 one (J&K and NE States) is technically a fifth.

37-052.r: Proportional representation → represents all groups (ethnicity, gender, interests, ideologies), so it eases minority representation; A and R true, R explains A.

37-054.r: Proportional representation is not needed where a two-party system has developed.

37-055.r: Lower turnout than last time → neither re-election nor cancelling non-voters' rights follows; voting is a statutory right and EC uses awareness campaigns.

37-056.r: Order → EVM (19 May 1982, Parur, Kerala) → Voter photo ID card (1993) → VVPAT (4 September 2013, Nagaland) → NOTA (SC order 27 September 2013).

37-057.r: VVPAT/EVM version used in India → M3, third-generation; holds data of 384 candidates; tamper detection and self-diagnostics.

37-058.r: Election Commission first made three-member in 1989 (two extra ECs, 16 October 1989 to 1 January 1990); three members again since 1 October 1993.

37-059.r: Not an ECI member → N.B. Lohani. In 2000: CEC M.S. Gill; ECs T.S. Krishnamurti and J.M. Lyngdoh, both later CECs.

37-060.r: First CEC → Sukumar Sen (21 March 1950 to 19 December 1958); only woman to head ECI → V.S. Ramadevi → both statements correct.

37-061.r: First woman Chief Election Commissioner → V.S. Ramadevi (1990). First CEC → Sukumar Sen (1950 to 1958).
37-061.h: Rama-DEVI: the 'Devi' who headed the Election Commission.

37-062.r: National Voters' Day → 25 January (Election Commission's foundation day), celebrated since 25 January 2011 to draw young voters.

38-001.r: Parties registered under RPA 1951 by Election Commission; National party → recognised in four or more states (among other tests); 1999 polls: six national, 48 state parties → all correct.

38-002.r: Recognition as National or State party → Election Commission, under Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.

38-003.r: Political parties are registered and recognised by the Election Commission of India (Election Symbols Order, 1968).

38-005.r: National party → any one: 2% Lok Sabha seats from three states; or 6% votes in four states + four Lok Sabha seats; or State party in four states.
38-005.c: No answer printed: none of the options (5% votes, contesting everywhere, power in four States) matches these conditions.

38-008.r: State party (Symbols Order 1968) → any one: 3 Assembly seats or 3%; 1 Lok Sabha seat per 25; 6% votes + seats; or 8% of total State votes.
38-008.t: UPPSC's key said 'None of the above'; the book holds 8% (option c).

38-010.r: 'National' in the name Indian National Congress → influenced by reaction against British rule.

38-011.r: Nationalist Congress Party → formed 10 June 1999 by Sharad Pawar, P.A. Sangma, Tariq Anwar after expulsion from Congress over Sonia Gandhi's foreign origin.

38-012.r: Muslim League, RSP, Forward Bloc, Peasants and Workers Party → none national. Six national parties now: BJP, INC, BSP, AAP, CPI(M), National People's Party.

38-013.r: Trinamool Congress (TMC) → given National party status on 2 September 2016; no longer a National Party now.

38-014.r: First BJP President → A.B. Vajpayee (1980). Bharatiya Jana Sangh founder → Shyama Prasad Mukherjee; BJP is its successor.

38-015.r: Not a national party → Samajwadi Party (formed 4 October 1992, Lucknow, by Mulayam Singh Yadav).

38-016.r: Regional political party → Akali Dal (Shiromani Akali Dal) of Punjab; Congress, BJP, CPI are not regional.

38-017.r: Not a national party → Telugu Desam Party, a regional party of Andhra Pradesh.

38-018.r: Aam Aadmi Party (when asked) → a state-level and registered party, so 'More than one of the above'; now it is a national party.

38-019.r: Independent Labour Party → founded by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar in August 1936.

38-020.r: Ambedkar founded → Independent Labour Party (1936), Scheduled Castes Federation (1942), Depressed Classes Federation (1930), Samata Sainik Dal; not Peasants and Workers Party (1948, Maharashtra).

38-021.r: Correct pairs: Bharatiya Jana Sangh → S.P. Mukherjee (1951); Congress for Democracy → Jagjivan Ram (1977). Swatantra Party → C. Rajagopalachari; Socialist Party → Acharya Narendra Dev.

38-022.r: Year of formation → CPI 1920 (Tashkent; in India 1925, Kanpur); CPM 1964; AIADMK 1972; Telugu Desam 1982.

38-023.r: Year of formation → Indian National Congress 1885; Bharatiya Jan Sangh 1951; CPI 1925; AIADMK 1972.
